newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 7.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The long-awaited restructuring of the 25 billion rand electricity supply industry has moved up a gear after Minerals and Energy Affairs Minister Penuell Maduna announced that the cabinet had finally approved proposals to transform the industry.
- The government has set the end of the year as target date to exorcise an estimated 47,000 "ghost workers" in the public service who are costing taxpayers up to five billion rand a year.

- Education Minister Sibusiso Bengu announced on Thursday that the tertiary education budget for 1997/98 would increase 11 percent or 49.1 million rand, but denied he had yielded to pressure from students following countrywide campus unrest.

- A High Court application by sister newspapers Business Day and The Sunday Times for access to controversial in-camera evidence by former defence force chemical warfare expert Wouter Basson has resulted in the partial release of his testimony.

- Barlow was involved in preliminary talks which could result in the indstrial holding company making an offer for the remaining 21.1 percent of London-listed subsidiary J.Bibby & Sons Plc, the group said.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Two companies refused to sign a Consumer Electronics Association document presented to the customs and excise department aimed at establishing minimum values for various electronic imports in an attempt to erase rampant under- valuation scams.
- Gazankulu Gold Fields (Gazgold), a liquidated gold mining company in the Northern Province, is soon to enter a new phase under a restructuring scheme.
- Anglovaal, the industrial and mining group, reported a 30 percent surge in attributable earnings to 308.9 million for the six months to December 31.

- Investors are buying defaulted African debt, according to research supplied by Investec Securities. Many investors are buying the debt instruments that African govenrments have already stopped paying, in the hope that such governments might recover and need more loans.

- The Mpumalanga Gaming Board revealed this week that Southern Sun's size influenced its decision to select Tsogo Sun as the preferred finalist for a gambling licence in Nelspruit. Southern Sun holds 50 percent of Tsogo.
SAKE-BEELD
- Mining and industrial group Anglovaal reported earnings of 488 cents per share in the six months to end- December -- 28 percent up on the 381 cents attained in the last half of 1995.
- The price of water might be increased by up to 60 percent later this year to carry the cost of the government's new water supply projects.
- The government's programme of affirmative action in the civil service will have to change in the wake of a court ruling on the programme earlier this week.

- First National Bank allegedly gave positive references for a company wanting further credit, even when it knew the company was insolvent and was not in a position to settle its existing debts, according to court papers.

- The Constitutional Court rejected provisions of the Criminal Procedure Act which held that company directors accused of an offence be deemed guilty unles they prove they did not participate and could not have stopped the offences in question. - - - -
THE STAR
- After two days of drenching rains, Gauteng residents can look forward to a relatively dry and sunny weekend with just a 20 percent chance of thundershowers.
- South Africa's tertiary institutions are owed at least 300 million rand in unpaid tuition fees and loans, and the Education Ministry said the number of students refusing to pay fees was growing.

- Morale at the state broadcaster plummeted with the circulation of a report recommending the closure of its breakfast TV programme, its production section, the dubbing department and the language bureau by end-April.

- Justice Minister Dullah Omar expressed support for and welcomed back to South Africa multimillion rand fraud accused Allan Boesak. Omar welcome him back in his capacity as the acting leader of the African National Congress in the Western Cape province.
